name: Cessna 425/441 Conquest
variants: Cessna 425 Conquest I / Corsair (Pratt & Whitney Canada PT6A turboprops)
summary: Pressurized twin turboprop from the Cessna 400-series piston-twin family, flown as a corporate and air-taxi aircraft; the 441 uses Garrett engines and the smaller-nacelled 425 uses PT6As.

engines: Two turboprops on the wing with long, slim nacelles
Large propeller spinners with three- or four-blade props
fuselage: Pressurized round-section cabin with small oval windows
Long, pointed nose with a sloping windshield
Stair door on the left rear of the cabin
tail: Tall swept fin with a dorsal fillet

tellTales: Small oval cabin windows on a low-wing twin turboprop with a conventional (non-T) tail
Long, slim engine nacelles carrying turboprops on a pressurized-looking, round cabin
Long pointed nose with a gently sloping windshield

confusedWith.howToTell: The 340/414/421 has piston engines with stub exhausts and a slightly smaller airframe; the Conquest has turboprop cowlings with big spinners and a larger, longer fuselage.
The King Air 90 has larger rounded-square windows and a blunter, bulkier cabin; the Conquest has small oval windows and a longer, more tapered nose.
The Cheyenne has a Navajo-style cabin with larger squarish windows and usually wingtip tanks; the Conquest has small oval windows and a more tapered, rounder cabin.
